title: Monetary Policy Report, July 13, 2018

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve submitted its July 2018 Monetary Policy Report to Congress, reaffirming its dual mandate of maximum employment and stable prices (2% PCE inflation target). The document states the median FOMC participant estimate for longer-run normal unemployment is 4.6 percent. The Committee commits to a balanced approach when employment and inflation objectives are not complementary. Source data extends through Q1 2018 and was publicly available as of July 12, 2018. Note: This record covers the introductory sections only (transmittal letter, statement on longer-run goals and monetary policy strategy).
key_points: FOMC reaffirms 2 percent inflation target measured by annual change in the PCE price index
Maximum employment level is not specified as a fixed goal due to nonmonetary factors affecting labor market structure and dynamics
Median estimate of longer-run normal unemployment rate among FOMC participants is 4.6 percent
Policy decisions reflect longer-run goals, medium-term outlook, and assessments of balance of risks including financial system risks
Balanced approach is used when employment and inflation objectives are not complementary, accounting for magnitude of deviations and different time horizons
Forward guidance language emphasizes symmetric treatment of inflation above and below the 2 percent objective
why_it_matters: This quarterly report establishes the Federal Reserve's official policy framework and strategic principles as of mid-2018. It documents the Fed's commitment to a 2% symmetric inflation target, which anchors long-term inflation expectations. The stated longer-run unemployment estimate of 4.6% provides a benchmark for assessing labor market slack. This document serves as a foundational reference for understanding Fed policy intentions and communication strategy. Historical record from July 2018.
macro_context: As a quarterly Monetary Policy Report submitted to Congress pursuant to section 2B of the Federal Reserve Act, this document provides the official framework for monetary policy. It describes the Fed's commitment to price stability (2% PCE inflation symmetric target) and its flexible approach to maximum employment. The balance of risks assessment and the dual mandate framework described here inform the trajectory of monetary policy decisions during the reported period. Historical document from mid-2018.
